source_text: Cur ergo dubitemus dicere, quod scriptura non dubitat exprimere? cur haesitabit fidei ueritas, in quo scripturae numquam haesitauit auctoritas? ecce enim Osee prophetes ait ex persona patris: 2am non saluabo eos in arcu, neque in equis, neque in equitibus; sed saluabo eos in domino deo ipsorum. si deus saluare se dicit in deo, non autem saluat nisi in Christo deus, cur ergo homo dubitet Christum deum dicere, quem deum a patre animaduertit positum per scripturas esse? immo si non saluat nisi in deo pater deus, saluari non poterit a deo patre quisquam, nisi confessus fuerit Christum deum, in quo se et per quem se repromittit pater salutem daturum; ut merito quisquis illum agnoscit esse deum, salutem inueniat in deo Christo; quisquis non recognoscit esse deum, salutem perdiderit, quoniam alibi nisi in Christo deo eam inuenire non poterit. Quo modo enim Esaias: ecce uirgo concipiet et pariet jilium, et uocabitis nomen eius Emmanuel, quod interpretatum est nobiscum deus, sic Christus ipse dicit: ecce ego uobiscum sum usque ad consummationem saecule, deus, immo multo magis etiam in nobis est. nobiscum est Christus: est ergo cuius nomen est nobiscum deus, quia et nobiscum est. aut numquid non est nobiscum? quo modo ergo dicit se nobiscum esse? est ergo nobiscum: sed § quoniam nobiscum est, Emmanuel, id est, nobiscum deus, dictus est. deus ergo quia nobiscum est, nobiscum deus dictus est. idem prophetes: conualescite, manus dissolutae, et genua debilia; consolamini pusillanimes sensu, conualescite, nolite timere: ecce deus noster iudicium retribuet: ipse ueniet et saluabit nos: tunc aperientur oculi caecorum, et aures surdorum audient; tunc saliet claudus sicut ceruus, et diserta erit lingua mutorum. si in aduentu dei dicit prophetes haec futura signa, quae facta sunt, aut dei filium agnoscant Christum, in cuius aduentu et a quo haec sanitatum signa facta sunt: aut diuinitatis Christi ueritate superati, in alteram haeresim ruentes, Christum dum filium dei et deum confiteri nolunt, patrem illum esse confiteantur. uocibus enim prophetarum inclusi iam Christum deum negare non possunt. quid ergo respondent, cum in aduentu dei haec signa futura dicuntur, quae in aduentu Christi gesta sunt? Christum qualiter accipiunt deum (deum enim iam negare non possunt), qua patrem aut qua filium? si qua filium, cur dei filium deum negant? si qua patrem, cur eos non sequuntur, qui eiusmodi blasphemias tenere uidentur? nisi quoniam nobis in hoc aduersus illos de ueritate certamine hoc interim sufficit, ut quocumque genere conuicti Christum confiteantur et deum, quem etiam deum negare uoluerunt. Per Abacuc prophetam ait: deus ab Africo ueniet et sanctus de monte opaco et condenso. quem uolunt isti ab Africo uenire? Si uenisse aiunt omnipotentem deum patrem, ergo de loco deus pater uenit, ex quo etiam loco cluditur, et intra sedis alicuius angustias continetur; et iam per istos, ut diximus, Sabelliana haeresis sacrilega corporatur, siquidem Christus non filius sed pater creditur: et nouo more, dum ab istis destricte homo nudus asseritur, per eos rursum Christus pater deus omnipotens comprobatur. at si in Bethlehem, cuius metaturae regio ad meridianam respicit plagam caeli, Christus nascitur, qui per scripturas et deus dicitur, merito deus hic ab Africo uenire describitur, quia a Bethlehem uenturus esse praeuide- ’ batur. eligant ergo ex duobus quid uelint hunc, qui ab Africo uenit,—filium esse, an patrem: deus enim dicitur ab Africo uenturus. si filium, quid dubitant Christum et deum dicere? deum enim scriptura dicit esse uenturum. si patrem, quid dubitant cum Sabellii temeritate misceri, qui Christum patrem dicit? nisi quoniam, siue illum patrem siue filium dixerint, ab haeresi sua inuiti licet desciscant necesse est, qui Christum hominem tantummodo solent dicere, dum illum, rebus ipsis coacti, deum incipiunt promere, siue dum illum patrem, siue dum illum filium uoluerint nuncupare.
pass_a_gloss: Why therefore should we doubt to say what scripture does not doubt to express? Why will the truth of faith hesitate, in which the authority of scriptures has never hesitated? For behold, the prophet Hosea says in the person of the Father: I will not save them by bow, nor by horses, nor by horsemen, but I will save them in the Lord their God. If God says He will save in God, and yet does not save except in Christ God, why therefore does man doubt to call Christ God, whom God the Father has noted through scriptures to be established as God? Indeed, if the Father God does not save except in God, no one will be able to be saved by God the Father unless he has confessed Christ to be God, in whom and through whom the Father promises to give salvation; so that deservedly whoever recognizes Him to be God may find salvation in God Christ; whoever does not recognize Him to be God will have lost salvation, because he will not be able to find it anywhere except in Christ God. For how does Isaiah say: Behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son, and you will call his name Emmanuel, which is interpreted as God with us? So Christ Himself says: Behold, I am with you until the end of the age, God, or rather much more even in us. Christ is with us, therefore He is the one whose name is God with us, because He is with us. Or does He not exist with us? How therefore does He say that He exists with us? He exists with us, but since He is with us, He is called Emmanuel, that is, God with us. Therefore, because He is with us, He is called God with us. The same prophet says: Be strong, you with disabled hands, and you with weak knees; comfort yourselves, you of little sense, be strong, do not fear: behold, our God will repay judgment, He Himself will come and save us; then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear; then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will speak. If the prophet says that these signs will occur at the coming of God, which have been done, either they should acknowledge Christ as the Son of God, in whose coming and from whom these signs of healing have been done; or, overcome by the truth of Christ's divinity, they should fall into another heresy, refusing to confess Christ as the Son of God and God. For they can no longer deny that Christ is God, enclosed as they are by the words of the prophets. What therefore do they respond, when these signs are said to be future at the coming of God, which have been done at the coming of Christ? How do they accept Christ as God (for they can no longer deny that He is God), as Father or as Son? If as Son, why do they deny that the Son of God is God? If as Father, why do they not follow those who seem to hold such blasphemies? Unless it is because for us, in this contest of truth against them, it is enough for now that they, convinced by any means, confess Christ to be God, whom they also wanted to deny as God. Through the prophet Habakkuk, it is said: God will come from Africa and the Holy One from the mountain opaque and dense. Whom do they want to come from Africa? If they say that the omnipotent Father God has come, then God the Father has come from a place, from which He is also enclosed, and is contained within the narrowness of some seat; and already, through them, as we have said, the sacrilegious Sabellian heresy is confirmed, since Christ is believed to be not the Son but the Father; and in a new manner, while they assert that man is naked and separate from God, through them Christ is again confirmed to be the omnipotent Father God. But if Christ, who is said through scriptures to be God, is born in Bethlehem, whose region lies towards the southern part of the sky, deservedly God is described as coming from Africa, because He was foreseen to come from Bethlehem. Let them therefore choose from two options what they want this one, who comes from Africa, to be - either the Son or the Father: for God is said to come from Africa. If the Son, why do they doubt to call Christ God? For scripture says that God is coming. If the Father, why do they doubt to mix with the temerity of Sabellius, who says that Christ is the Father? Unless it is because, whether they call Him Father or Son, they must necessarily depart from their heresy, although unwilling, who are accustomed to call Christ only a man, while they begin to proclaim Him as God, either when they want to call Him Father or when they want to call Him Son.

pass_b_english: Why should we hesitate to speak what Scripture declares without doubt? Why should the truth of faith waver when Scripture's authority has never wavered? The prophet Hosea speaks in the Father's own voice: 'I will not save them by bow, nor by horses, nor by horsemen, but I will save them in the Lord their God' (Hosea 1:7). If God says He will save in God, yet saves only in Christ God, why does anyone hesitate to call Christ God? The Father has established Him as God through Scripture. Indeed, if the Father God saves only in God, no one can be saved by the Father unless he confesses Christ as God. The Father promises to give salvation in Him and through Him. Therefore, whoever recognizes Him as God finds salvation in God Christ; whoever refuses to recognize Him loses salvation, because it cannot be found anywhere except in Christ God.

Consider how Isaiah says: 'Behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son, and you will call his name Emmanuel, which means God with us' (Isaiah 7:14). Christ Himself says: 'Behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age'—God, or rather, even more intimately, God in us. Christ is with us; therefore He is the One whose name is God-with-us, because He truly is with us. Or is He not with us? How then can He say He is? He is with us, and precisely because He is with us, He is called Emmanuel, that is, God with us. So He is called God with us because He is God and He is with us.

The same prophet cries: 'Strengthen the feeble hands, steady the knees that give way; take courage, you of little faith, be strong, do not fear: behold, our God will repay judgment; He Himself will come and save us. Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute sing for joy' (Isaiah 35:3-6). If the prophet says these signs will happen at the coming of God, and they have happened, then either they must acknowledge Christ as the Son of God—in whose coming and by whose power these healings were done—or, overcome by the truth of Christ's divinity, they must fall into another heresy by refusing to confess Christ as Son of God and God. The words of the prophets hem them in; they can no longer deny that Christ is God. What answer can they give? These signs were foretold for the coming of God, yet they occurred at the coming of Christ. How do they receive Christ as God—for they can no longer deny His deity—as Father or as Son? If as Son, why do they deny that the Son of God is God? If as Father, why do they not follow those who hold such blasphemies? Unless it is enough for us, in this present contest for truth, that they stand convicted by any argument and confess Christ as God—even they who wanted to deny His divinity.

Through the prophet Habakkuk it is said: 'God comes from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran' (Habakkuk 3:3). Whom do they say comes from Africa? If they claim the omnipotent Father God has come, then God the Father has come from a place—meaning He is confined to a location and contained within the limits of some seat. Through them, as we have shown, the sacrilegious Sabellian heresy takes shape: Christ is believed to be not the Son but the Father. And in a new twist, while they insist that Christ is merely a naked man, separate from God, they actually prove again that Christ is the omnipotent Father God. But if Christ, whom Scripture calls God, is born in Bethlehem—whose region lies toward the southern quarter of the sky—then rightly God is described as coming from Africa, because He was foreseen to come from Bethlehem. So let them choose between two options: will this One who comes from Africa be the Son or the Father? For Scripture says God is coming. If He is the Son, why do they hesitate to call Christ God? Scripture says God is coming. If He is the Father, why do they shrink from embracing the rashness of Sabellius, who says Christ is the Father? Unless it is because, whether they name Him Father or Son, they are forced—however unwillingly—to abandon their heresy. They are accustomed to calling Christ only a man, yet the facts compel them to proclaim Him as God, whether they call Him Father or Son.

review.notes: Pass B fails on scripture citation accuracy and translation fidelity regarding the Habakkuk passage. 1. Pass B cites 'Hosea 1:7' for 'I will not save them by bow...', but the Latin text (and the actual scripture) is Hosea 1:7 (or 2:17 in some traditions), however, the provided notes/lemmas and the Latin text itself are being checked against the translation. More critically, Pass B translates 'deus ab Africo ueniet et sanctus de monte opaco et condenso' as 'God comes from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran' (Habakkuk 3:3). While this is the standard biblical text, the instructions state: 'A summary is not a translation' and 'Pass A must preserve every clause's sense; B must neither add to nor contradict A or the Greek [Latin]'. Pass B replaces the specific Latin words 'ab Africo' and 'monte opaco et condenso' with 'Teman' and 'Mount Paran'. While this is a 'correct' biblical identification, it is a departure from the provided Locked Latin text which specifically uses 'Africo' and 'opaco et condenso'. Pass B's choice to use the standard biblical wording instead of the provided Latin text constitutes a failure to translate the supplied source. 2. Pass B's citation of Hosea 1:7 is technically a mismatch for the content if the user expects the translation of the provided Latin 'ex persona patris: 2am non saluabo eos...' which is Hosea 2:17 (often 1:7 in older numbering), but the primary failure is the substitution of the Habakkuk text.
reasons: Pass B substitutes the Latin 'ab Africo et sanctus de monte opaco et condenso' with 'from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran', which is a departure from the provided source text 'deus ab Africo ueniet et sanctus de monte opaco et condenso'.
